directAnswer: Pelagius I was pope from 556 to 561. A Roman deacon who had represented the papacy in Constantinople, he first opposed and then accepted the condemnation of the Three Chapters, and Emperor Justinian chose him to succeed Vigilius. As pope he faced distrust in the West, worked to restore the finances of the Roman church after the Gothic War, and began the church of Santi Apostoli.

sections.h2: Deacon, Diplomat, and Defender of Rome
paras: Pelagius, from a Roman family, served as papal representative in Constantinople and influenced Justinian's condemnation of Origenist teachings in 543. During the Gothic siege of Rome in 546, he used his own wealth to feed the starving population and negotiated with the Gothic king Totila, who sent him to Constantinople on a peace mission.

He initially sided with Western opposition to condemning the Three Chapters and wrote a defense of them. After the Second Council of Constantinople, he changed his position, and Justinian, recognizing his ability, chose him to succeed Vigilius.

Pelagius returned to Rome in 556, where many clergy and laypeople blamed him for Vigilius's hardships and doubted his orthodoxy. Few bishops would consecrate him; the Liber Pontificalis says only two bishops and a priest from Ostia took part. He made a public oath at St. Peter's that he had done no harm to Vigilius, and declared his loyalty to the four ecumenical councils.

Bishops in northern Italy and parts of Gaul remained distrustful, and the sees of Milan and Aquileia broke communion over the Three Chapters. Pelagius reorganized the papal estates, restored church administration, and aided the poor after years of war. He began the church of Santi Apostoli in Rome, completed by his successor. Pelagius died in March 561 and was buried at St. Peter's.

keyFacts: Fed starving Romans during Totila's siege in 546
Chosen by Emperor Justinian after accepting the condemnation of the Three Chapters
Began the church of Santi Apostoli in Rome

faqs.question: Why was Pope Pelagius I distrusted when he became pope?
faqs.answer: He had shifted his position on the Three Chapters and was suspected of involvement in Vigilius's mistreatment. To answer those doubts, he swore a public oath at St. Peter's and affirmed his loyalty to the four ecumenical councils.

faqs.question: Did Pope Pelagius I build Santi Apostoli?
faqs.answer: He began the church of Santi Apostoli in Rome, and it was completed under his successor, John III.
